meta.name: reconcile
meta.description: 128 F-reconciliation (jav/reconcile.py): which bank statement line paid which incoming invoice, by code. The invoice types, the payment window, the signal thresholds, the payment channels, the pairs listed for their equal amount alone, the names learnt from a person's confirmations, the payment kinds left to a person, when a statement counts as verified coverage and how a candidate's strength is weighed. Decisions: DECISIONS 128 (exact amount and at least one signal first; card payments with an exchange rate later; never 'unpaid'), DECISIONS 131, DECISIONS 134.

changelog.note: 136 E4 (DECISIONS 132, 136): statement_types also takes statement_table, an account's statement read by code from a bank's tabular export (jav/statement_table.py, jav/flow_statement_table.py); its lines are paired like an extracted statement's.

134 (DECISIONS 134, pre-matching by code): signals.fuzzy_name - a distinctive word of the supplier's name (cut after its legal form, without numbers, min_chars letters at least) that begins a word of the line's name, or the other way round when the line's word holds min_prefix_share of it (a name cut short on a card terminal), or differs from it by about a letter (min_ratio), or is the same whole word leading the supplier's name (its brand), is the weak supplier_name_fuzzy signal; it alone ties only an equal amount; a word in the names of common_min suppliers, or of common_min lines making common_share of the different line names, ties nothing. invoice_fields.references - the customer id, customer code, order and contract number matched in the memo like the invoice number (the reference signal). invoice_fields.payment_account is a list: a utility bill names the supplier's account supplier_bank_account. strength - the weights of a candidate's 0-100 strength (signals, amounts, booked by the due date plus grace_days or only in the window): an order and a reason on the pairing page, not a threshold.

133 (DECISIONS 133, the own parties): invoice_fields.buyer_name and buyer_tax_id - the buyer side of an invoice, read into the snapshot so a reconciliation package shows its own party's invoices (jav/parties.py); the pairing itself does not use them.

131 E1 (DECISIONS 131, the reconciliation package): line_marks - the reasons a person gives for a statement line that needs no invoice (a private expense, a bank fee or interest, a transfer between own accounts, a tax or contribution, a cash withdrawal, a salary, other with a note).

131 (DECISIONS 131): invoice_fields.payment_method; payment_channels (the postal cheque: an invoice payable by cheque and a line through a cheque payment app are tied by the payment_channel signal; patterns on the normalised, accent-free text, document vocabulary); amount_only (a line with exactly an invoice's amount in one currency, in its window, without a signal, is listed for a person, never proposed); learning.min_confirmations (a person's confirmation ties the line's counterparty name to the supplier, the learned_name signal; a payment app line teaches nothing).

130 K3: card payments of foreign-currency invoices (DECISIONS 128 variant C, second half). A forint line of a credit card statement and an invoice in another currency form a candidate when a signal ties them and the line falls in fx.window around the issue date; the invoice amount is converted at the MNB rate of the issue date (jav/fx.py) and the pair is proposed when the line is within policy.json reconcile.fx_tolerance. Without a known rate the pair is listed, not proposed (status rate_missing). The card accounts also count in the coverage of a foreign-currency invoice.

128 K1: first version. Rules ported selectively from the legacy project's orchestrator/framework/payables.py 0.1.1 (10_AIFLOW_V4 HEAD 4256cba): the reason-coded exclusions, the signals and 'an equal amount alone is no candidate'. New: the exact-amount rule, the window's upper end, coverage by verified statements.
